newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end slightly up in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end slightly up in cautious trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed slightly up Tuesday in low volume as investors showed caution ahead of possible U.S. interest rate rises making bonds more attractive than emerging market equities, brokers said. They added prices would probably remain broadly stable Wednesday.

Tuesday, the General Index rose 0.43 percent to 1,651.68 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index edged up 0.13 percent to 2,370.62 points. In a total of 1,237 trades, volume was a meager 21.0 million soles ($8.0 million), according to preliminary figures.
"Investors are pretty calm ahead of the rates decision. The market should not be affected very much," said Flavio Campos of local brokerage Finanval.

Players have assumed the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike rates so that the market has adjusted to this as if the rise has already been announced, brokers said. But without knowing the size of the rise, investors preferred to play safe Tuesday, they added.
Among blue chip stocks, benchmark Telefnica del Per "B" closed Tuesday up 0.17 perecnt at 5.89 soles in volume of 680,000 shares.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa - formerly known as Edegel - rose 0.81 percent to 1.24 soles, on volume of 917,000 shares.
Brewer Compania Nacional de Cerveza closed down 1.43 percent at 1.38 soles in volume of 982,000 shares.
